Emma — thanks for the upload and the failure examples. Below is the recommended shortlist and our rationale. I’ve also attached a short PDF with the micro-benchmarks and the prompt samples we’ll run (redwood_model_shortlist_v1.pdf, eval_prompt_samples.jsonl).

Shortlist (recommended for your triage workload)
1) RW-instruct-7B-q4
   - Quality: Strong instruction-following and lower hallucination rate for short responses. Best cost-to-quality for intent classification.
   - Latency (typical p50 on Redwood hosted, 256 tokens): ~45–70 ms per token start (warm) — end-to-end for 256 tokens ~80–140 ms median; p95 ~350–500 ms depending on routing and prefix caching.
   - Cost: lowest unit cost (ideal for high QPS).
   - Risk: May underperform on very long chained reasoning; include regression prompts.

2) Llama-3-13B-int8 (Redwood-optimized runtime)
   - Quality: Noticeably better at multi-step instructions and reduced looped hallucinations vs 7B.
   - Latency: p50 ~120–180 ms for 256 tokens; p95 ~450–900 ms (depends on backend and batch configuration).
   - Cost: ~2–2.5x 7B cost per token. Good midpoint for quality without full 70B expense.
   - Risk: Slightly higher token consumption for verbose responses; we’ll enforce max tokens and structured output prompts to contain cost.

3) RW-realtime-13B-int8 (low-latency variant) — conditional recommendation
   - Quality: Comparable to Llama-3-13B on many instruction tasks; tuned for latency.
   - Latency: p50 ~90–140 ms; p95 ~260–420 ms with dedicated pool and prefix caching.
   - Cost: similar to Llama-3-13B but with higher infra reservation (reserved capacity recommended).
   - Use-case: When 95th percentile latency target is strict (<400ms) and you can commit to dedicated capacity.

Notes on 70B-class models
- 70B and larger models give quality gains for extremely complex multi-step summarization, but at a >5x incremental cost and much higher latency (p95 often >1s). For triage use-case they don’t provide proportional uplift for intent classification.

Evaluation plan we propose
- Run the uploaded NovaHealth sample set through the three candidate models with the attached prompt set (eval_prompt_samples.jsonl).
- Metrics: intent F1, hallucination rate (defined in the primer), token usage, and latency (p50/p95). We’ll produce a short report with per-example highlights and failure clusters.
- Regression checks: include your supplied corner cases plus an automated differential test that flags examples where the candidate’s output deviates from the baseline behavior above a similarity threshold.

Quick answers to your explicit asks
- p95 SLA: Based on our internal runs, RW-realtime-13B-int8 on reserved capacity meets a 4s SLA easily and will often be in the sub-500ms p95 range for 256-token responses. The standard Llama-3-13B-int8 on shared pools can spike near or over 1s p95 depending on queueing.
- Regression risks moving 7B -> 13B: Usually improves instruction-following and factuality, but you should expect occasional shifts in phrasing and tokenization differences that change exact outputs. That’s why we include regression sets and prompt-locking rules during rollouts.

Deliverables by EOD tomorrow
- Full per-example benchmark report (Drive link)
- A short script to run locally against Redwood hosted endpoints (we’ll include example API calls and prompt templates)
- Suggested rollout plan: canary (5%), 25%, 100% with automated rollback on F1 drop >2.5 points.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_model_shortlist_v1.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: eval_prompt_samples.jsonl (JSONL)]
